dish: Char koay teow — flat rice noodles seared over intense charcoal wok-hei with prawns, cockles and Chinese sausage
n: Penang Road Famous Jin Kor Char Kuey Teow
address: Lebuh Keng Kwee (off Jalan Penang), George Town, Penang, Malaysia
w: ~40-year charcoal stall in the Penang Road cendol lane; MICHELIN Guide-listed for its cockle-and-prawn char koay teow with pronounced wok hei.

dish: Nasi kandar — steamed rice flooded with a mix of curries (kuah campur) and the legendary fried chicken
address: 177 Jalan Penang (alley at Lebuh Chulia junction), George Town, Penang, Malaysia
w: Penang's most legendary 24-hour nasi kandar, cooked in a narrow lane since the 1940s; the 'flooded' curry-mix rice and fried chicken are institutions.

dish: Penang asam laksa — sour tamarind-and-mackerel rice-noodle soup with torch ginger, mint and shrimp paste
address: Beside Air Itam Market, Jalan Pasar, Air Itam, Penang, Malaysia
w: The definitive Air Itam asam laksa; CNN Travel ranked Penang asam laksa among the World's 50 Best Foods. Reopened after a pandemic pause; now weekends only.

dish: Nga choy kai — poached chicken with crunchy Ipoh bean sprouts and silky hor fun in the local alkaline-water style
address: Jalan Yau Tet Shin, Ipoh, Perak, Malaysia (relocating to a larger nearby space in 2026)
w: Ipoh's iconic tauge ayam since 1957 — poached chicken, blanched bean sprouts and smooth hor fun. Anthony Bourdain ate here; still open, moving to a bigger site in 2026.

dish: Nasi lemak with ayam goreng berempah — coconut rice, sambal and spice-crusted fried chicken
address: 5 Jalan SS21/37, Damansara Utama (Uptown), Petaling Jaya, Selangor (Greater KL), Malaysia
w: The nasi lemak many call Malaysia's best; queues since the 1980s for the ayam goreng berempah. Regulars have included prime ministers and national athletes.

dish: Chicken rice balls — Hainanese poached chicken with rice hand-rolled into ping-pong-sized balls, sweet-chilli and ginger
address: 18 Jalan Hang Jebat (Jonker Street), Malacca, Malaysia
w: The long-queued Jonker Street original of Malacca's signature rice-ball chicken rice, at the entrance to Jonker Walk; documented by Mark Wiens and in the MICHELIN Guide's chicken-rice feature.

dish: Khai jiao poo — a fat charcoal-fried crab omelette packed with a full pound of crab meat
address: 327 Maha Chai Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
w: Bangkok's one-MICHELIN-star street stall; octogenarian chef Supinya 'Jay Fai' Junsuta cooks in ski goggles over charcoal. Held its star since 2018; now open Wed–Sat.

dish: Pad thai — charcoal-fired rice noodles wrapped in a thin egg crepe (pad thai hor kai)
address: 313-315 Maha Chai Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
w: The 'Pad Thai Pratu Phi' institution near the Grand Palace, cooking over charcoal since 1966; MICHELIN Guide-recommended and a fixture of every Bangkok food tour.

dish: Khao niao mamuang — glossy coconut sticky rice with ripe mango
address: 431-433 Tanao Road, Phra Nakhon, Bangkok, Thailand
w: An 80+-year family sticky-rice shop near the Grand Palace; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand for its mango sticky rice.

dish: Kuay jub nam sai — peppery clear-broth rolled rice-noodle soup with crispy pork belly
n: Nai Ek Roll Noodle (Nai Ek Kuay Jub)
address: Soi Yaowarat 9, Yaowarat (Chinatown), Bangkok, Thailand
w: A Chinatown Bib Gourmand mainstay for aggressively peppery rolled-noodle soup and crispy pork.

dish: Khao soi kai — northern coconut-curry egg noodles with braised chicken, topped with crispy noodles
address: 29/1 Ratchaphuek Alley, Chang Phueak, Chiang Mai, Thailand
w: One of Chiang Mai's most famous khao soi houses; MICHELIN Guide-listed, with chicken and beef versions.

dish: Khao soi — the locals' benchmark bowl, perfectly balanced coconut curry noodles (lunch only)
address: Near Wat Kuan Kama, Sithiwongse Road, Old City, Chiang Mai, Thailand
w: The tiny lunch-only stall locals most often name as Chiang Mai's best khao soi; also a Mark Wiens pick.

dish: Pho bo — clear long-simmered beef broth, rice noodles and brisket, eaten with youtiao
address: 49 Bat Dan Street, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi, Vietnam
w: Hanoi's most famous old-school beef pho — order at the counter and queue; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand.

dish: Bun cha — charcoal-grilled pork patties and belly in sweet-sour nuoc cham with rice vermicelli (the 'Combo Obama')
address: 24 Le Van Huu Street, Hai Ba Trung District, Hanoi, Vietnam
w: The 'Obama bun cha' where Barack Obama and Anthony Bourdain dined in 2016 (Parts Unknown); now in the MICHELIN Guide Vietnam.

dish: Banh mi thap cam — an overstuffed baguette of house pate, cold cuts, butter and pickles
address: 26 Le Thi Rieng Street, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: Saigon's most famous banh mi since 1989 — permanent queues for the thap cam loaded with pate and cold cuts.

dish: Com tam suon — broken rice with a marinated grilled pork chop, egg meatloaf and pickles
address: 84 Dang Van Ngu Street, Phu Nhuan District, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
w: A Bib Gourmand com tam house famous for its thick, well-charred grilled pork chop over broken rice.

dish: Banh mi — Bourdain's 'symphony in a sandwich', crackly baguette with pate, char siu and herbs
address: 2B Phan Chau Trinh, Hoi An Ancient Town, Quang Nam, Vietnam
w: Made world-famous when Anthony Bourdain filmed here and called it a 'symphony in a sandwich'; the definitive Hoi An banh mi.

dish: Babi guling — Balinese spit-roast suckling pig stuffed with turmeric, lemongrass and chilli
address: Jl. Tegal Sari No. 2 (off Jl. Suweta, near Ubud Palace), Ubud, Bali, Indonesia
w: Ubud's most famous babi guling, from a recipe once cooked for the royal family; made globally famous by Anthony Bourdain. Lunch only, until the pork runs out.

dish: Sate ayam / kambing — chicken and mutton satay with rich peanut sauce
address: Jl. Kebon Sirih Raya (original branch), Central Jakarta, Indonesia
w: The original outlet of Jakarta's best-known satay house; a reliable, Lonely Planet-recommended introduction to Indonesian classics.

dish: Gudeg — sweet young-jackfruit stewed for hours in coconut milk and palm sugar, with chicken and egg
address: Jl. Wijilan (near the Kraton), Yogyakarta, Indonesia
w: Yogyakarta's most famous 'dry' gudeg, run since ~1950; the benchmark for the city's signature dish.

dish: Rendang & nasi padang — slow-cooked dark beef rendang served the tower-of-dishes Padang way
address: Jl. Blora, Central Jakarta, Indonesia
w: A respected Padang restaurant since 1973; its rendang landed it on Asia's 50 Best 'Essence of Asia'.

dish: Cebu lechon — herb-stuffed, no-MSG whole-roast pig with shatteringly crisp skin ('the best pig, ever')
address: One Mango Avenue (and branches), Cebu City, Philippines
w: The Cebu lechon Anthony Bourdain declared 'the best pig, ever' on his Philippines episode; founded by food writer Joel 'Marketman' Binamira.

dish: Spicy Cebu lechon — the chilli-and-lemongrass 'spicy' style Rico's pioneered
address: F. Cabahug Street, Mabolo (and branches), Cebu City, Philippines
w: Cebu's most internationally recognised lechon brand and pioneer of the spicy style, open since 1997.

dish: Chicken barbecue — grilled marinated chicken with java rice and the house peanut sauce
address: 432 San Andres Street cor Roxas Boulevard, Malate, Manila, Philippines
w: A Manila institution since 1936, 'home of the best chicken barbecue in town'; its Roxas Blvd home is a National Historical Commission-marked historic site.

dish: House crispy sisig — deep-fried, chopped pork sisig, a modern-classic version
address: Ayala Triangle Gardens, Makati (flagship; branches across Metro Manila), Philippines
w: The Moment Group's beloved Filipino comfort-food chain; its flagship carries a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand and its crispy sisig is a signature.

dish: Mohinga — Myanmar's national catfish-and-lemongrass rice-noodle soup; also lahpet (tea-leaf salad)
address: 77-79 Pansodan Street (Lower Block), Yangon, Myanmar
w: A restored colonial-era tea house downtown, widely loved for a polished mohinga and tea-leaf salad.

dish: Seasonal Khmer tasting menu — river fish, fermented pastes and fresh herbs, incl. a refined take on amok
address: Sala Kamreuk (Wat Damnak area), Siem Reap, Cambodia
w: Cambodia's most-awarded kitchen — a seasonal Khmer degustation applying French-trained rigour to local produce (ranked in OAD's Leading Restaurants of Asia).

dish: Fish amok — coconut-and-kroeung fish curry steamed in banana leaf
address: 74 Street 174, Phnom Penh, Cambodia
w: Country-style Khmer cooking (famous fish amok) in a French-colonial villa; a Friends International social enterprise training at-risk youth.

dish: Laap & Lao tasting platter — minced-meat laap, jeow dips, mok pa and Luang Prabang sausage
address: Kingkitsarath Road (Nam Khan riverside), Luang Prabang, Laos
w: Luang Prabang's best-known 'Lao cuisine' restaurant and cooking school; a guided introduction to laap, jeow and the Lao sampling platter.
